messages:
Lina: Heads-up — nightly perf on main shows a 10% tail latency regression for short prompts after yesterday's runtime change. noticed it on the small-prompt test (concurrency=1).
Omar: Ugh. Which change landed? any specific CL?
Lina: The kernel-selector rewrite + new batching heuristic landed in a single PR (git sha f3a9d2b). It changes the default policy to prefer throughput kernels for batches >= 4.
Kai: Short prompts at concurrency=1 are mostly batch size 1/2, so could be picking the wrong kernel variant. :thinking:
Priya: Do we have traces? nvprof/nsys/perfetto?
Lina: Pushed two traces to s3: s3://redwood-traces/2100456789/before.nsys and s3://redwood-traces/2100456789/after.nsys. Also uploaded a perfetto heatmap: https://perfetto.example/trace/2100456789-heatmap
perf-bot: Automatic regression alert created: reg-2100456789. Latency +10% (p95) on small-prompt benchmark.
Marco: Quick look at the perfetto heatmap shows repeated 1-2ms gaps between kernel launches in the after trace around t=120-140s. That's likely scheduler jitter + wrong kernel path.
Omar: Can you paste the nsys timeline snippet?
Lina: snippet from nsys flame: ```
# after.nsys (timeline sample)
GPU  0: launch kernel A_variant_throughput  time 0.45ms
GPU  0: wait                                 time 1.80ms
GPU  0: launch kernel B_variant_latency     time 0.30ms
GPU  0: wait                                 time 1.60ms
```
Kai: That wait time between launches looks like kernel warmup / context switch. If the kernel selector switches between variants per-request, we get fractured pipelines.
Priya: Could be KV-cache cold path as well — if the KV cache causes path lengthening we might be switching to a fallback kernel that checks cache tags.
Omar: Repro steps request: Lina can you paste the exact bench command?
Lina: repro command: ``python bench/latency.py --model redwood-v1-small --prompts 1000 --concurrency 1 --seq_len 64 --profile nsys --server dedicated-gpu-2``
Marco: I ran the same locally and saw similar pattern. I also profiled with nvtx markers — the marker after token 8 shows a selector call per token. That's the smoking gun.
Kai: OK plan: bisect PRs between commit before selector rewrite and the new one. Use the bench harness with --profile nsys and compare the kernel timeline.
Omar: I'll start a git bisect. commands: ``git bisect start HEAD f3a9d2b^ f2741c8`` then run the bench script and mark good/bad.
Lina: FYI, I reproduced locally with `--kernel-policy=latency-first` and the regression disappears. So default policy change is strongly implicated.
Priya: That suggests we changed the default without a safety check for low-batch scenarios. We should update selector to consult runtime batch size distribution (if mean_batch < 3 prefer latency kernels).
Kai: For immediate mitigation we can flip default back and ship a hotfix flag. Patch: `runtime/config.cc` change default to LATENCY_PRIORITIZE when avg_batch < 4.
Marco: I created a small patch branch that sets the policy via env var RW_KERNEL_POLICY, tested on nightly pool, p95 back to baseline. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/compare/fix/selector-default
Omar: Running bisect now, I'll attach trace snippets per commit to s3 so we can grep for inter-launch gaps. Script I'm using: ``./tools/bisect_perf.sh --start 2023-11-01 --end HEAD --bench small_prompt``
perf-bot: Bisect job queued (job id bisect-2100456789).
Lina: Evergreen: please collect both timeline (nsys) and nvprof with `--nvprof --nv-disasm gpu` to see kernel names and launch patterns.
Kai: If bisect homes in on the selector rewrite, I'll add a regression test that runs microbench with batch=1,2 and asserts kernel variant stability (no alternating kernels within a single sequence).
Priya: Also add a KV-cache warmup check in CI so cache-dependent paths are exercised. A tiny synthetic workload to fill KV for a few prefixes should do.
Omar: Update: bisect narrowed it to 3 commits. Attaching the after trace for the first bad commit: s3://redwood-traces/2100456789/bisect/bad-commit-1.nsys
Marco: I diffed the kernel name sequence between good/bad and see pattern: good: [lat_k, lat_k, lat_k...] bad: [thr_k, wait, lat_k, wait, thr_k] — selector returning throughput kernel intermittently.
Lina: Good find. Let's ship the env-var hotfix and keep bisect running for root cause. I'll open an incident PR to revert default in main and add a test.
Kai: I'll own the test and follow-up fix to selector heuristics. Omar continue bisect until we have exact patch.
Omar: Will do. ETA 2h to finish bisect and upload final traces.
Lina: Thanks everyone — update the incident with links to traces and patch. End state: short-prompt tail regressed due to kernel selection policy change; mitigation hotfix via env var revert; longer term selector heuristics update + CI microbench.
